details: Heightened geopolitical instability, particularly renewed military exchanges between the U.S. and Iran, has fueled a "risk-off" sentiment across financial markets. This macroeconomic factor has significantly impacted the cryptocurrency market, leading to a broad sell-off. Bitcoin (BTC) has retreated below $73,000, and the overall crypto market capitalization saw a substantial decline of approximately $80 billion within 24 hours due to institutional de-risking.

details: Spot Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) have recorded significant net outflows, with one day witnessing $733.4 million in outflows, marking the largest single-day withdrawal since January. Over the past two weeks, total outflows have exceeded $2.5 billion, indicating a meaningful reversal of the earlier inflow trend and a clear signal of institutional investors reducing their exposure to the asset class.

details: Ethereum (ETH) has fallen below the psychologically important $2,000 level for the first time since March, experiencing declines of over 5% in the last 24 hours and nearly 8% over the past week. Record open interest in Ether futures, coupled with falling spot prices, suggests an increase in aggressive leveraged short positioning in the market. This downturn is further attributed to a deteriorating fundamental narrative for Ethereum, with institutions reportedly retreating as the attractiveness of staking yields decreases compared to rising U.S. Treasury yields.
